newsitem.title: FRANCE: CAP ponders 737QC for scheduled cargo charter.
newsitem.headline: CAP ponders 737QC for scheduled cargo charter.

text.p: French airline, Continent Air Paris (CAP) said it was considering replacing its ATR 42, which operates a scheduled cargo charter service on behalf of French express distribution company, Extand, with a bigger aircraft later this year.

"We'll soon be taking delivery of a Boeing 737-200QC (quick change) aircraft which will be based in Palma, Majorca from where it will operate passenger charter services exclusively during the forthcoming tourist season running from April to October," a CAP offfical told Reuters.

After this period, CAP planned to base the 737-200QC in Toulouse where it would be available for passenger charters during the day and converted to full-freighter configuration for night-time cargo charters, the official said.
"We are discussing with Extand the possibility of using the aircraft, which can carry around 12 tonnes of cargo per flight, on a Toulouse-Marseille-CDG-Marseille-Toulouse rotation."
CAP's 4.8 tonne capacity ATR 42 currently operates a nightly route between Paris and Marseille service carrying Extand shipments.
"Extand's HQ is in Toulouse so there would appear to be scope for extending the routing of its air cargo service but we are still at the project stage for the moment."
